findings.finding: The state model does not explicitly handle `triageError` or `reminderCorruptLines`. A parseable v1 response containing either could become an `ok` response with no items, incorrectly suggesting nothing is due. Aggregation also needs to preserve individual project failures.
findings.suggestion: Define these states explicitly, retain their diagnostics, and test both per-project and mixed-success all-project responses. Validate all ten item fields at runtime before accepting a v1 answer.

findings.finding: The plan omits the required shared `cli-child-spawn.ts` helper and does not establish how the runner resolves the project’s main checkout. These are explicit requirements; using the server working directory or a selected worktree could operate on the wrong store.
findings.suggestion: Specify shared spawn-helper reuse and main-checkout resolution from registered project metadata. Test invocation from a worktree and ensure any triage runner changes preserve its existing behavior.

findings.finding: “Exit 2 refused passes message through” does not establish unchanged refusal text or the required no-retry behavior. Generic output trimming, stderr decoration, or shared retry handling could violate that contract.
findings.suggestion: Pin the actual CLI refusal behavior in a test: assert the exact exposed message and exactly one invocation. Confirm the CLI distinguishes refusal from ordinary argument-validation failures before treating every exit 2 as refusal.

findings.suggestion: Inspect representative stored commands read-only, record the observed resume syntax for the operator, and preserve command values as opaque text throughout the bridge.
